title: Choir and Oath Anew
premise: Rosalind Dravenmoor has spent fifteen years guarding the Hollow Gate, the last sealed door into Vaelith, a kingdom erased from every map and memory except hers. When a mute child arrives speaking Old Vaelish, Rosalind realizes the gate is leaking — and that the exiled king's oath-bound warden is hunting the child to finish what the kingdom's fall began. To save her, Rosalind must re-enter the drowned country of her own buried past, confront the bargain she made to survive its destruction, and choose between reopening the gate for a people who no longer exist or sealing it forever with herself on the wrong side. In the end she gives up her memories of Vaelith to power the seal, keeping only the child — and a single, unexplained habit of humming an old choir tune.
about_author: Theo Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border-town folklore before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about doors, debts, and the people paid to keep both.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. A routine winter of bribes and closed roads at the Hollow Gate is interrupted when a girl of eight appears in the snow, barefoot, unafraid, singing in a language Rosalind hasn't heard since childhood. The emotional beat is dread disguised as competence: Rosalind recognizes the song and lies to her own deputy about why.

chapters.title: What the Child Said
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The child, Wren, cannot speak the common tongue but draws maps of streets that shouldn't exist — the capital of Vaelith, which Rosalind remembers burning. A passing merchant recognizes one sketch and flees without paying. Beat: grief resurfacing; Rosalind begins sleeping with a knife.

chapters.title: A Man Made of Oaths
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The warden Corvane arrives under a flag of parley, courteous and terrible, claiming Wren is stolen royal property and that Rosalind swore an oath he intends to collect. She denies everything; he leaves a black iron token on her table. Beat: the past arrives wearing a polite face, and Rosalind's authority cracks.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind, interleaved with memory. Flashbacks reveal the fall of Vaelith: Rosalind was the choir-keeper's daughter who opened a side door for refugees and was paid in survival and silence. Present-day: her deputy finds the token and asks questions. Beat: guilt made structural — we see exactly what her quiet cost.

chapters.title: The Road That Isn't There
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Corvane's soldiers close in; Rosalind takes Wren through smuggler roads that bend toward Vaelith whether she wills it or not — the country is pulling them. Wren speaks her first common word: Rosalind's name, in the old pronunciation. Beat: flight becoming pilgrimage; reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: The Drowned Capital
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. They cross into Vaelith proper: a city frozen mid-moment, snow falling upward, ghosts rehearsing a choir that never finished its last anthem. Rosalind meets the ghost of her mother, who does not forgive her. Beat: awe curdling into reckoning; the price of survival named aloud.

chapters.title: Corvane's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Corvane. His chapter reveals his truth: he bound himself to the oath that destroyed Vaelith to stop a plague-god wearing the king's face, and Wren is that god's seed, innocent and growing. He offers Rosalind mercy if she surrenders the child. Beat: antagonist humanized; certainty shaken on both sides.

chapters.title: The Choir Assembles
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Wren, terrified of what she's becoming, asks Rosalind to teach her the anthem — not to unleash it but to finish it, closing the loop. Ghosts gather; Corvane's army breaches the gate behind them. Beat: hope chosen against evidence; motherhood in all but blood.

chapters.title: Anthem for a Dead Kingdom
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Climax. In the ruined cathedral, Rosalind conducts the unfinished anthem while holding the gate shut against Corvane's power. The song demands payment in memory: every recollection of Vaelith, offered voice by voice by the ghosts and finally by her. Corvane, hearing his own name sung back as absolution, breaks his oath and lets the seal complete. Beat: sacrifice, release, and the god-seed dissolving into music rather than conquest.

chapters.title: Keeper of Nothing
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Spring. Rosalind remembers almost nothing of why she hums an old tune, only that the girl beside her matters more than any missing thing. The Hollow Gate stands sealed; her deputy keeps the ledger now. Final beat: bittersweet peace — survival's price paid at last, and worth it, though she'll never know the full sum.
